usageNotes: Use this to permanently remove an LVM thin pool from a node; the target node must be online and the caller must hold Sys.Modify at the root path (plus Datastore.Allocate on /storage when using cleanup-config). The operation returns an async task UPID — poll the task status to confirm completion before treating the pool as removed. If VMs or containers still reference volumes inside the thin pool, removal will fail; evacuate or remove those volumes first.

examples.summary: Remove thin pool 'data-thin' from node 'pve1', clean up storage config and wipe underlying disks

destructiveReason: Permanently destroys the LVM thin pool and all virtual disk volumes it contains; data is unrecoverable unless a backup exists, and cleanup-disks will additionally wipe the underlying block devices.
tips: cleanup-config removes the storage definition from Proxmox; omit it if you plan to recreate the pool under the same name and want to preserve the storage entry.
cleanup-disks wipes partition/signature data so the physical disk can be reused — skip this flag if you intend to repurpose the VG for another thin pool without re-partitioning.
The required volume-group param must match the VG that contains the thin pool, not the thin pool name itself.
Always snapshot or back up any VM/CT disks stored in the pool before calling this endpoint.
